Subject: Incident summary & next steps — 2026-11-22 partial hosted generation outage

Hi Daniel — thanks again for the quick signal and for sharing logs. Below is a brief incident summary and next steps; our full postmortem and remediation plan are linked.

What happened
- Between 10:45–11:05 PST on 2026-11-22, a subset of the us-west-2 hosted generation pool experienced transient kernel panics during a rolling quantized-kernel rollout. This caused elevated tail latency and a 503 rate peaking at ~14% for traffic routed through affected nodes.

Customer impact
- PillarSys observed ~12% failed calls for EU-origin requests routed through our us-west-2 edge during the window; some requests returned truncated outputs. No data loss; requests either failed quickly (503) or succeeded.

Immediate remediation taken
- Engineering paused the kernel rollout within 8 minutes of detection and rolled back to the prior kernel.
- Capacity reallocation shifted traffic to healthy nodes and to the us-east replica; autoscaler burst policy was temporarily widened to reduce queuing.

Root cause (short)
- A regression in a quantized attention kernel exposed an edge-case when running with a specific request batch size distribution (seen in PillarSys traffic pattern). The rollout lacked a canary for that request-profile.

Action items / timeline
- RDW-5498: Add request-profile canaries to kernel rollout logic (assigned to Marcus Lin) — ETA 2026-12-03.
- Improve rollout observability for tail latency signals (Irene Choi) — ETA 2026-12-07.
- Customer credit proposal: 10% service credit for the impacted hour; Stephanie will follow up with formal billing note.

Links & artifacts
- Postmortem: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/2026-11-22-pillar-fallback
- Engineering ticket: JIRA RDW-5498
- Support reference: HubSpot hs_123456789
- Attachments: postmortem-summary.pdf (summary), client-logs-clip.txt (from customer)
